Event loop, call stack, tasks and
microtasks

The call stack executes JavaScript. Tasks include events and timers; promise reactions are microtasks. At a
microtask checkpoint, microtasks drain before the next task. Rendering may occur between tasks.
Main code එක call stack එJක් run Jවනවා. Timer callback task queue එකට යනවා. Promise reaction microtask queue එකට යනවා. Stack එක හිස් වූ පසු microtasks මුලින් run කරලා ඊළඟ task එකට යනවා.
A UI displays output from synchronous code, promises and timers.
Call stack: A, D Microtasks: C Tasks: B · Output: A D C B
Read the diagram: Call stack: A, D. Microtasks: C. Tasks: B. Output: A D C B.
පළමුව stack එJක් A සහ D, පසුව microtask C, අවසානJයේ timer task B. එම පිළිJවළ output එJක් Jපන්වනවා.
Expected result: A, D, C, B.
Interview question: Why does C run before B?
Answer: The promise reaction is a microtask and runs at the checkpoint before the next timer task.
